hero.title: The Parthians (Pahlavas) in India
hero.description: A study of the Indo-Parthian dynasty that ruled North-Western India post-Mauryan era, bridging the gap between Greeks and Kushanas.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The Indo-Parthian timeline spans the 1st Century BCE to the 1st Century CE.

cards.details: Gondophares I establishes the Indo-Parthian kingdom in the Kabul valley and Indus region.
Takht-i-Bahi inscription evidence of Gondophares' rule; arrival of St. Thomas legend.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Remember the key players in the Indo-Parthian transition.

items.title: G.A.P
items.decryption: Gondophares is the most important king; associated with Apostle Thomas, and represents the Pahlavas.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse Pahlavas (Parthians) with Pallavas of Kanchi (South India). They are geographically and chronologically distinct.
The Indo-Parthians did not rule vast Indian territories like the Kushanas; their influence was localized to the North-West.

deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Arachosia, Drangiana, and Indus Valley
  • Capital: Taxila (Sirkap)

Personalities

  • Vonones: First ruler
  • Gondophares I: Most powerful king

Key Historical Mindmap

  • Origins
    • Iranian tribal roots
    • Successors to Indo-Greeks in the Northwest
  • Administration
    • Satrapal system (Kshatrapas)
    • Feudalistic decentralization
  • Religious Impact
    • Patronage of Buddhism
    • Legend of St. Thomas: Conversion of Gondophares
FeatureIndo-Parthians
Primary SourceTakht-i-Bahi Inscription
NumismaticsBilingual coins (Greek/Kharosthi)
